title: Region-aware SLA bundles & credits — packaging questions
text:
Region-aware SLA bundles & credits — packaging questions

['From: Elena Martinez <elena@orbitalhealth.com>\\nTo: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>\\nDate: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00\\nSubject: Region-aware SLA inquiry and credits\\n\\nHi Kimberly,\\n\\nThanks for the conversation last week — Orbital Health is evaluating Redwood for a multi-region inference deployment and we need clarity on how SLA and premium support packaging would work across regions. Two quick asks to start:\\n\\n1) How do you price and package uptime tiers when we require active-active failover between US-East and EU-West? Specifically, are there distinct \\"failover credits\\" or a blended tier?\\n2) What\'s the typical discounting approach for a 12–18 month commit at ~$1.2M ARR? We need a clear view of response windows, escalation coverage (onsite vs remote — we expect remote triage + callback), and how credits would apply if failover triggers a cross-region switchover.\\n\\nCan you put together an initial packaging suggestion and a sample pricing worksheet?\\n\\nThanks,\\nElena Martinez\\nHead of Platform Engineering\\nOrbital Health\\n\\nAttachment: usage_profile_q1_2027.csv (text/csv)', 'From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>\\nTo: Elena Martinez <elena@orbitalhealth.com>\\nDate: 2027-04-11T09:34:00-07:00\\nSubject: Re: Region-aware SLA inquiry and credits\\n\\nElena —\\n\\nAppreciate the clear asks. I\'ve started a draft pricing worksheet and a short note on packaging options (attached). High level — we typically do:\\n\\n- Blended availability tiers: single SLA applied to the committed footprint, with a built-in cross-region failover allowance (the \\"failover buffer\\").\\n- Failover credits: applied when a failover causes sustained increased consumption above the buffer for >30 minutes; credits scale by excess token-hours and a pre-agreed multiplier depending on severity.\\n- Response windows: Standard (8x5), Priority (24x7), and Premium (24x7 with on-call retainer). Escalation coverage mapping is configurable per-region.\\n\\nI\'ll attach: Orbital_SLA_Pricing_worksheet_v3.xlsx and a compact term sheet. Could you send a short summary of expected peak concurrency and whether you need on-prem private endpoints in EU region? That will change the pricing materially.\\n\\nIf useful, we can set a 30-min sync tomorrow to run through the workbook.\\n\\nBest,\\nKimberly Park\\nSenior Sales Manager, Enterprise\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\nAttachment: Orbital_SLA_Pricing_worksheet_v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)\\nAttachment: redwood-sla-term-sheet.pdf (application/pdf)', 'From: Elena Martinez <elena@orbitalhealth.com>\\nTo: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>\\nCc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@orbitalhealth.com>\\nDate: 2027-04-11T11:07:00-07:00\\nSubject: Re: Region-aware SLA inquiry and credits\\n\\nKimberly —\\n\\nThanks, received both attachments. Quick clarification on our side:\\n\\n- Peak concurrency is ~1,600 vCPU-equivalent inference sessions, sustained bursts to ~3,500 for up to 45 minutes.\\n- Monthly token volume estimate ~120M tokens.\\n- We will not be running on-prem in EU initially — everything will be cloud-based but we require EU data residency for EU-region model keys.\\n- Primary ask: a 12-month commitment. Our procurement team wants to understand the magnitude of \\"failover buffer\\" and the crediting thresholds (so they can evaluate risk).\\n\\nCan Karthik or finance give a sample calculation that converts a failover event into an expected credit figure? Also: what discount band should we expect for this TCV?\\n\\nCheers,\\nElena\\n\\nOn Mon, Apr 11, 2027 at 9:34 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:\\n> Elena —\\n> \\n> Appreciate the clear asks. I\'ve started a draft pricing worksheet and a short note on packaging options (attached). High level — we typically do:\\n> \\n> - Blended availability tiers: single SLA applied to the committed footprint, with a built-in cross-region failover allowance (the \\"failover buffer\\").\\n> - Failover credits: applied when a failover causes sustained increased consumption above the buffer for >30 minutes; credits scale by excess token-hours and a pre-agreed multiplier depending on severity.\\n> - Response windows: Standard (8x5), Priority (24x7), and Premium (24x7 with on-call retainer). Escalation coverage mapping is configurable per-region.\\n> \\n> I\'ll attach: Orbital_SLA_Pricing_worksheet_v3.xlsx and a compact term sheet. Could you send a short summary of expected peak concurrency and whether you need on-prem private endpoints in EU region? That will change the pricing materially.\\n> \\n> If useful, we can set a 30-min sync tomorrow to run through the workbook.\\n> \\n> Best,\\n> Kimberly Park\\n> Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise\\n> Redwood Inference', "From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>\\nTo: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Elena Martinez <elena@orbitalhealth.com>\\nCc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@orbitalhealth.com>\\nDate: 2027-04-12T08:22:00-07:00\\nSubject: Fwd: Region-aware SLA inquiry and credits — request for sample credit calc and discount band\\n\\nTeam — looping you in for pricing calc and discount guidance. Key details from Orbital: 1.2M ARR target/12-month commit, monthly ~120M tokens, peak concurrency up to 3.5k for short bursts, cloud-only (EU residency required).\\n\\nProposed approach (draft):\\n- Option A (Conservative): 99.95% blended uptime across committed footprint, built-in failover buffer = 10% of committed consumption per region, failover credits apply to excess >10% sustained >30m. Estimated credit exposure per 1 hour failover event = 0.5% of monthly committed spend (example numbers in attached worksheet).\\n- Option B (Premium): 99.99% with a dedicated retainer (on-call) + 24x7 priority support; smaller failover buffer (5%) and quicker escalation SLA. Price uplift +12% to +18% depending on retainer size.\\n\\nAsking Finance: Laura — can you produce a sample failure-to-credit calculation using their volumes and give us a discount band for TCV ~1.2M (what's realistic for an enterprise pilot -> committed rollout)?\\n\\nElena — we'll get a calculation back by EOD tomorrow and propose two concrete SKU packs. If that looks good, we can get a pilot addendum and DocuSign ready.\\n\\nThanks,\\nKim\\n\\nAttachment: Orbital_SLA_Pricing_worksheet_v3.xlsx\\nRelated: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ORBITAL-1245", 'From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>\\nTo: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Elena Martinez <elena@orbitalhealth.com>\\nCc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@orbitalhealth.com>\\nDate: 2027-04-12T16:05:00-07:00\\nSubject: Re: Fwd: Region-aware SLA inquiry and credits — request for sample credit calc and discount band\\n\\nKim/Karthik/Elena —\\n\\nAttached is a short worked example (sheet tab \\"CreditCalc\\") using Orbital\'s token volumes and peak concurrency. Key takeaways:\\n\\n- Using Option A assumptions, a 2-hour sustained cross-region failover that pushes consumption 18% above buffer would translate to approximately 1.1% credit on that month\'s invoice (~$11,000 on a $1M monthly run-rate equivalent). The credit escalates non-linearly if failover persists beyond 4 hours.\\n- Option B reduces exposure materially (example shows ~0.2% credit for same event) due to the larger retainer and faster triage.\\n- Discounting: For a 12-month, $1.2M ARR commit, we can offer an ELA-style band: 10% standard discount + up to 5% for annual payment and technical onboarding credit (total up to 15%). For pilot-first then convert to commit within 90 days, we can offer a 7% pilot discount and an execution credit applied at conversion.\\n\\nIf Orbital needs an even firmer cap on credit exposure we can structure a capped credit reserve (pre-funded retainer) at an incremental cost.\\n\\nLaura Bennett\\nDirector, Finance — Redwood Inference\\n\\nAttachment: Orbital_SLA_Pricing_worksheet_v3.xlsx (updated with CreditCalc tab)', 'From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>\\nTo: Elena Martinez <elena@orbitalhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>\\nDate: 2027-04-13T15:42:00-07:00\\nSubject: Re: Region-aware SLA inquiry and credits — next steps\\n\\nElena — thanks for the details and thanks Laura for the calc. To be pragmatic:\\n\\n- Proposal: Start with a 3-month pilot (7% pilot discount) scoped to US + EU with Option A packaging and a capped credit exposure via a $25k pilot-recovery retainer.\\n- On successful pilot metrics (latency/availability and failover behaviour), convert to 12-month committed ELA with 12% baseline discount + 3% accelerated payment credit (total 15%) and optional on-call retainer for Premium OPTION B if you want tighter exposure.\\n- We\'ll prepare a pilot addendum and a full-term sheet for the commit phase; DocuSign links can be shared once Orbital confirms the pilot SKU.\\n\\nIf that aligns I\'ll have legal prep the addendum and Kimberly will coordinate signatures.\\n\\nKarthik Iyer\\nHead of Sales — Enterprise\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\nOn Tue, Apr 12, 2027 at 4:05 PM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com> wrote:\\n> Kim/Karthik/Elena —\\n> \\n> Attached is a short worked example (sheet tab \\"CreditCalc\\") using Orbital\'s token volumes and peak concurrency. Key takeaways:\\n> \\n> - Using Option A assumptions, a 2-hour sustained cross-region failover that pushes consumption 18% above buffer would translate to approximately 1.1% credit on that month\'s invoice (~$11,000 on a $1M monthly run-rate equivalent). The credit escalates non-linearly if failover persists beyond 4 hours.\\n> - Option B reduces exposure materially (example shows ~0.2% credit for same event) due to the larger retainer and faster triage.\\n> - Discounting: For a 12-month, $1.2M ARR commit, we can offer an ELA-style band: 10% standard discount + up to 5% for annual payment and technical onboarding credit (total up to 15%). For pilot-first then convert to commit within 90 days, we can offer a 7% pilot discount and an execution credit applied at conversion.\\n> \\n> If Orbital needs an even firmer cap on credit exposure we can structure a capped credit reserve (pre-funded retainer) at an incremental cost.\\n> \\n> Laura Bennett\\n> Director, Finance — Redwood Inference', "From: Elena Martinez <elena@orbitalhealth.com>\\nTo: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>\\nCc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@orbitalhealth.com>\\nDate: 2027-04-13T16:05:00-07:00\\nSubject: Re: Region-aware SLA inquiry and credits — next steps\\n\\nKarthik/Team —\\n\\nThat package looks workable. We accept the 3-month pilot with the 7% pilot discount and the $25k pilot-recovery retainer to cap credit exposure. Please proceed with a pilot addendum and DocuSign; procurement needs the exact SKU and the term sheet to sign off.\\n\\nNext steps we need from Redwood:\\n- Pilot addendum (DocuSign) with SKU and failover buffer defined\\n- Finalized pricing worksheet showing the pilot numbers and conversion discount mechanics\\n- Contact for technical kick-off (we'll want an SRE onboarding session in week 1)\\n\\nThanks — looking forward to getting started.\\n\\n—Elena\\n\\nOn Tue, Apr 13, 2027 at 15:42 Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:\\n> Elena — thanks for the details and thanks Laura for the calc. To be pragmatic:\\n> \\n> - Proposal: Start with a 3-month pilot (7% pilot discount) scoped to US + EU with Option A packaging and a capped credit exposure via a $25k pilot-recovery retainer.\\n> - On successful pilot metrics (latency/availability and failover behaviour), convert to 12-month committed ELA with 12% baseline discount + 3% accelerated payment credit (total 15%) and optional on-call retainer for Premium OPTION B if you want tighter exposure.\\n> - We'll prepare a pilot addendum and a full-term sheet for the commit phase; DocuSign links can be shared once Orbital confirms the pilot SKU.\\n> \\n> If that aligns I'll have legal prep the addendum and Kimberly will coordinate signatures.\\n> \\n> Karthik Iyer\\n> Head of Sales — Enterprise\\n> Redwood Inference"]
